note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): Arab Bank, the Housing Bank and Capital Bank. Arab Bank Jordan's card pages give no prices and its fees page links no card tariff (its Reflect digital bank's card, read on 2026-10-29, is kept); the Housing Bank's site didn't answer this research's connections; Bank al Etihad's fees manual (7 October 2026) answered with a CloudFront block and wasn't read. Reflect, Arab Bank's digital bank in Jordan: its fees and commissions charge its credit card 1.5% a month in interest and nothing to apply for or issue, with no yearly fee among them. Capital Bank's rates and fees (the July 2026 edition, read in full on 2026-10-30): its credit cards in dinars, each free for its first year and then charged its primary card's annual renewal fee (Visa Platinum 50, Signature 70, Infinite 150, Infinite Privilege 500 dinars), waived when the year's purchases reach 2,000, 4,000, 6,000 or 10,000 dinars; its Visa Infinite in US dollars, euros, pounds, dirhams and riyals, each with its issuance or annual fee (200 dollars, euros or pounds; 750 dirhams or riyals), waived on a year's purchases of 15,000 dollars or pounds, 35,000 euros or 55,000 dirhams or riyals. Every card bears 1.5% a month on the outstanding balance; a cash advance costs 4%, at least 4 dinars (the floor written on the dinar cards only); the foreign currency conversion fee is 3% for all currencies and 4% for euro transactions (written as 3%, the game's card holding one share); the overline fee and the late payment fee are each 10 dinars a month, written on the dinar cards (on the foreign-currency cards a fee set in dinars isn't written). The fee for paying in dinars at a merchant abroad (1.5%) isn't written. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period.
